html:
The Otavalo are a Kichwa-speaking Indigenous people of Imbabura province in the northern highlands of Ecuador, around the town of Otavalo. They are famous worldwide as weavers and traders.

Before the Incas the region belonged to the Caranqui and their neighbours, who resisted the Inca advance for years. Tradition says that Huayna Capac had so many defenders killed at a lake near Ibarra that it was named Yahuarcocha, "lake of blood". Under Spanish rule the people were forced to work in textile workshops, the obrajes.

From that hard past came their modern trade. Since the mid 1900s Otavalo weavers have sold their cloth and knitwear in a famous Saturday market and in cities across the world, and many families became prosperous. Men wear a long braid as a mark of identity. They speak Kichwa, a form of Quechua. North of them live the Pastos.
sum: The Otavalo are a Kichwa-speaking Indigenous people of Imbabura province in the northern highlands of Ecuador, around the town of Otavalo. They are famous worldwide as weavers and traders.
